judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The X share link is a 30px circle holding only a white X glyph (SVG fill currentColor, #fff) on #4cc2ff; it has no visible text, only an aria-label and a hover title on its li. Pixels in the screenshot give #ffffff on #4cc2ff = 2.01:1, and the circle itself is 1.92:1 against the #fafafa page, so nothing else identifies the control at 3:1. Skeptic check: the logo exemption in Understanding 1.4.11 covers a logo presented in the brand's mandated colours, but X's logo is black or white and #4cc2ff is the Bricks theme's legacy 'twitter' colour (not even Twitter's #1DA1F2); a brand-compliant black X on this blue would pass, so this low-contrast presentation is an author choice and 'not essential' (Understanding, Figure 22 reasoning). The live page (fetched 2026-11-25) has the same markup (ul.brxe-post-sharing.brand-colors, aria-label only, title on the li) and the theme CSS frontend-layer.min.css still sets color:#fff on the list and the same brand background colours; the screenshot is fully styled, so the capture matches what users receive. The claim names the failure.

judgments.label: uncertain
judgments.rationale: The Telegram share link shows only Telegram's white paper-plane logo on a #54a9eb circle; pixels confirm #ffffff on #54a9eb = 2.55:1, so the sentence is true of the capture. Skeptic reason that holds up: Understanding 1.4.11 exempts brand logos presented in the brand's colours under the essential exception and says the exemption normatively 'carries over' to a component whose only visible content is the logo. #54A9EB is Telegram's own colour for its official share and login buttons (telegram.org widget-frame.css, a.tgme_widget_share_btn) and Telegram's logo is itself a white plane on a light-blue circle (about 2.6-3.0:1), so this low contrast comes from the brand, not the author. Auditors split on whether a third-party share icon gets that exemption, so whether it fails cannot be settled. The live page (fetched 2026-11-25) has the same markup (ul.brxe-post-sharing.brand-colors, aria-label only, title on the li) and the theme CSS frontend-layer.min.css still sets color:#fff on the list and the same brand background colours; the screenshot is fully styled, so the capture matches what users receive.
